title: A title typed over a video is readable without restyling it
goal: Press T over a recording and type, and the title comes out as small black regular text, 24 points on a 1280 wide picture, which disappears on the dark screen recordings people make. Premiere and Final Cut both start a title large, white and bold enough to read. The first title should read on video before anybody touches the Text section.
notes: Found by measure-the-video-editor-against-premiere-and-fi (2026-09-24); gap report docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md. Seen in an-editing-session-walk 6-title-at-b-sc.png (docs/design/video-vs-premiere/title-default-look.jpg): 'Ship it faster' 24 px SF Pro Regular, black, on the dark Sample Talk frame. foregroundFill #000000 in walk state. Mock video.html draws the title large, white, serif bold ('Ship it faster.').
acceptance: A title typed over a video at Next defaults is white (or picks a colour that reads against the frame under it), bold, and sized to the picture (about a twentieth of its height)
Text typed on a still picture keeps the look it has today
The editing-session walk's title picture shows the words readable at a glance
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on, and an audit written under queue/audits/ gives the try steps and a real picture
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
